Observation block 1.
Reservoir levels in the northern catchment fell 18 percent below the seasonal median during the observation window. (block 1, item 1)
Field sensors recorded soil moisture readings that were consistently in the lowest decile for this time of year. (block 1, item 2)
We interpret the combined readings as an early signal of hydrological stress rather than sensor drift. (block 1, item 3)
We recommend increasing the sampling interval from weekly to daily for the next two months. (block 1, item 4)
Sensor coverage in the eastern sub-basin is sparse, so the uncertainty of these estimates remains high. (block 1, item 5)
The recommendation should be revisited when the new telemetry stations come online in autumn. (block 1, item 6)

Observation block 2.
Stream turbidity spiked after each of the three storm events logged in March. (block 2, item 1)
Manual grab samples confirmed elevated suspended sediment concentrations at all four monitoring stations. (block 2, item 2)
The most plausible interpretation is accelerated bank erosion in the recently cleared corridor. (block 2, item 3)
A staged revegetation program for the cleared corridor is the recommended intervention. (block 2, item 4)
Because only one storm season has been observed, confidence in the erosion attribution is moderate at best. (block 2, item 5)
Follow-up transect surveys after the next storm season should trigger a review of this recommendation. (block 2, item 6)

Observation block 3.
Groundwater bores show a slow but persistent decline of roughly 0.4 meters per year across the plain. (block 3, item 1)
Pumping records from irrigation cooperatives indicate extraction grew 9 percent year on year. (block 3, item 2)
The decline is best explained by extraction outpacing recharge rather than by climatic variation alone. (block 3, item 3)
We recommend capping new extraction licenses until a full water balance study is completed. (block 3, item 4)
Recharge estimates rely on a regional model that has not been calibrated with local tracer data. (block 3, item 5)
The cap should be reassessed once the tracer study delivers calibrated recharge figures. (block 3, item 6)
